headline: Record Tanker Freight Rates Halt US Gulf Crude Oil Exports to Asia
summary: Oil tanker shipping rates from the US Gulf Coast to China surged to as high as $80 million, ten times historical averages, crippled by vessel shortages and inefficiencies tied to Middle East conflict.
why: Spiking tanker freight rates alter global arbitrage economics, stranding US crude in domestic markets while raising import costs for Asian refiners.

impacts.name: Oil Tanker Shipping
impacts.why: Crushed vessel availability and route inefficiencies pushed charter rates to historic highs.

impacts.name: Crude Oil
impacts.why: Arbitrage closures suppress US export demand while restricting crude supply into Asian import hubs.

why_moved: Severe vessel supply crunches driven by Middle East turmoil sent tanker rates to $80 million per voyage, making US Gulf exports to Asia commercially unviable.
